summary: Saved dashboard filters removed after customer plan upgrade; scheduled alerts lose tracehook links and usage credits mismatch
description:
Issue summary:
BrightHealth AI reported that following an account plan upgrade from 'dedicated' to 'enterprise' on 2026-03-07 the following symptoms were observed: saved dashboard filter presets for several teams were missing, scheduled alert notifications no longer contained valid tracehook links (links 404 or redirect to expired token), and a subset of hourly usage credits show negative adjustments in the billing export for the upgrade window.

Impact:
- Multiple product dashboards used for SLA monitoring returned to default filters causing missed incident context during a 2026-03-08 latency spike.
- Scheduled alerts that rely on tracehook links to attach trace context now send notifications with expired/invalid tracehook URLs; recipients cannot drill into traces from Slack/email.
- Billing report for 2026-03-07 22:00-23:59 shows -120 credit adjustments attributed to route attribution rekey during the upgrade. Customer is concerned about invoice accuracy.

Environment:
- Customer account: BrightHealth AI (enterprise)
- Region: prod | us-east
- Console version: web-ui v2.14.1 (served from CDN revision 20260306)

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Perform plan upgrade via billing console (dedicated -> enterprise) for org ID: org-1769 on 2026-03-07 21:34 UTC.
2) Open saved dashboards used by teams (SRE, ML Platform).
3) Validate saved filters and open scheduled alerts attached to those dashboards.
4) Click tracehook links in an alert delivery (Slack/email).
5) Download CSV usage export for 2026-03-07 window and inspect route-level credits.

Observed behavior:
- Saved dashboard filters were reset to defaults (filters removed from saved preset).
- Alert deliveries contain tracehook URLs that 404 or redirect to 'token expired'.
- CSV export shows negative adjustments for some routes during the upgrade period.

Expected behavior:
- Plan upgrade should not modify saved dashboard state or invalidate existing tracehook links. Billing/usage exports should not show negative adjustments without clear audit log entries.

Attachments/links:
- Customer-provided screenshot of dashboard filter list before/after (attached to ticket).
- Slack thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/support/threads/G01ABCDE123
- Billing export excerpt: s3://support-uploads/brighthealth/billing-20260307-excerpt.csv
- Relevant internal runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Org+Plan+Change+Runbook
comments: Support (Maya Chen) - 2026-03-08: Acknowledged with initial triage. Confirmed customer-reported timestamps and requested export + screenshots. Escalated to SRE due to tracehook expiry and billing anomalies.

SRE (Liam O'Connor) - 2026-03-09: Reproduced expired tracehook behavior in a staging org plan-change test. Hypothesis: migration job that re-keys org namespace rotates tracehook tokens without updating scheduled alert payloads. Collected logs from tracehook-service for org-1769 (log ids: thook-logs-1771).
Customer (BrightHealth Ops) - 2026-03-09: Confirmed team interruption impact during the latency spike, requesting a fast workaround to restore dashboard filters and trace link drilldowns.

Billing (Priya Rao) - 2026-03-10: Pulled billing ledger for org-1769; negative adjustments correlate to a reconciliation batch that attempted to reassign route-level credits after org tier change. Investigating whether a compensating transaction failed to apply.

Engineering (Eve Martinez) - 2026-03-11: Noted related PR that adjusted tracehook token TTL logic merged last month. Will validate interaction with migration scripts. Assigned a small rollback candidate to avoid immediate customer impact if needed.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-09: Reproduced on staging when running org-migration v1.8.2; saved dashboard metadata is stored under org-scoped keys and a migration path inadvertently dropped 'saved_filters' map when a legacy 'plan' flag is present.

Tracehook logs (thook-logs-1771) show token rotation events at 21:35 UTC with expired_token responses on subsequent alert deliveries. Token rotation occurred as part of 'rekey-org-namespace' job started by migration-controller.

Billing ledger shows 'reassign_credit' ops for routes r-1201,r-1207 that inserted negative adjustment rows before the final commit; final reconciliation failed due to a transient constraint violation (fk_route_org) when migration changed org_id mapping mid-transaction.
resolution_notes: Workaround (2026-03-11): Restored saved_filters from config-backups for affected dashboards for BrightHealth AI (restore snapshot snapshot-2026-03-07-21). Restored scheduled alert payloads by re-generating tracehook tokens and pushing a refresh to the alerting service for org-1769.

Temporary mitigation (implemented 2026-03-12): Disabled automatic tracehook token rotation inside the migration job for 'plan' changes until migration logic is updated. Added a guard to skip rewriting saved_dashboard metadata when legacy plan flag present.

Permanent fix plan: (1) Patch migration-controller to preserve 'saved_filters' map and perform route credit reassignment in an idempotent two-phase commit, (2) adjust tracehook token rotation to update references in the alerting queue atomically or issue token refresh callbacks to subscribers, (3) add unit/integration tests covering plan-upgrade migration with existing scheduled alerts and billing reconciliations. Target release: 2026-03-20 (eng sprint).

Follow-ups: Draft communication to BrightHealth AI account team summarizing root cause and credit reconciliation plan. Finance will prepare an invoice adjustment if reconciliation does not auto-correct.
